chapters.name: Sign Shapes, Colors, and Regulatory Signs
chapters.summary: What each sign shape and color tells you, and the red, white, and black signs that state rules you must obey.
keyPoints: The eight-sided sign always means stop. The triangle pointing down always means yield.
Regulatory signs state rules, such as speed limits, ONE WAY, DO NOT ENTER, and turn rules. A red circle with a slash means the action shown is not allowed.
Green signs guide you, blue signs show services, and orange signs mark construction and maintenance work.

chapters.name: Warning, School, Railroad, and Work Zone Signs
chapters.summary: Yellow diamond warning signs, school signs, railroad crossing signs, the no passing pennant, and orange work zone signs.
keyPoints: Diamond-shaped signs warn of a hazard or change in the road ahead, such as a curve, a merge, or a road that ends.
The five-sided sign means a school zone or school crossing. The round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.
Orange signs mark work zones. In a work zone, a flagger has the same authority as a regulatory sign.

chapters.name: Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: Steady and flashing lights, arrows, lane control and pedestrian signals, and what yellow and white lines on the road mean.
keyPoints: A flashing red light means stop, then go when it is safe. A flashing yellow light means slow down and go with caution.
If a signal is not working at all, treat the intersection as if there is a stop sign in every direction.
Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes going the same way. Use the center turn lane only for left turns.

chapters.name: Right of Way, Pedestrians, and Emergency Vehicles
chapters.summary: Who goes first at intersections and driveways, how to treat pedestrians, and what to do for school buses, emergency vehicles, and Georgia's Move Over law.
keyPoints: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
Stop for a school bus that has its red lights flashing and stop arm out. On a highway divided by a median, traffic going the other way does not have to stop.
For a stopped emergency, sanitation, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, move over a lane if you safely can. If not, slow down below the speed limit and be ready to stop.

chapters.name: Speed, Passing, and Parking
chapters.summary: Georgia's general speed limits, the Super Speeder law, safe passing, and the places where you may not park.
keyPoints: Unless posted otherwise, the limit is 30 mph in urban or residential districts, 35 mph on unpaved county roads, 70 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates and multi-lane divided highways, and 55 mph elsewhere.
A Super Speeder is a driver convicted of 75 mph or more on a two-lane road or 85 mph or more on any road. A $200 state fee is added.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, 30 feet of a stop sign or signal, or 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

chapters.name: Safe Driving and Sharing the Road
chapters.summary: Headlights, following distance, bad weather, skids, expressways, seat belts and child seats, the Hands-Free law, and sharing the road with bicycles, motorcycles, and trucks.
keyPoints: Use headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and whenever it is raining.
Give a bicycle at least 3 feet when you pass. Leave a motorcycle a full lane and follow it by three or four seconds.
Georgia's Hands-Free law says you may not hold or support a phone with any part of your body while driving.

chapters.name: Instructional Permit and Teen Licenses (TADRA)
chapters.summary: The Class CP instructional permit, the Class D provisional license, Joshua's Law, and the rules that limit teen drivers.
keyPoints: You can get a Class CP permit at 15. You may drive only with a licensed driver at least 21 years old sitting beside you.
For a Class D license you must be 16, hold the permit one year and one day, and complete 40 hours of supervised driving with 6 at night.
A Class D driver may not drive from 12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. Passenger limits change at six months and at one year.

chapters.name: DUI, Implied Consent, and Points
chapters.summary: Georgia's alcohol limits for adults and drivers under 21, the implied consent law, and the point system that can suspend your license.
keyPoints: A driver 21 or older is under the influence at 0.08 or more. A driver under 21 is under the influence at 0.02 or more.
Refusing a state chemical test suspends your license for at least one year.
Your license is suspended at 15 points in 24 months. A driver under 18 is suspended at 4 points in 12 months.
